target.title: fix(gateway): bound cross-boot restart-recovery with a persistent retry budget
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #95750.

When a channel main-session turn wedges and a restart marks the entry `abortedLastRun: true`, the next boot's recovery pass calls back into the same resume path **unconditionally**. The in-process orchestrator (`MAX_RECOVERY_RETRIES = 3`) only bounds retries *within a single process invocation* — the counter is never persisted, so each fresh boot is a fresh retry budget. The result is a deterministic death loop until `systemd`'s `StartLimitBurst` is exhausted and an operator must intervene.

This adds a **persistent, cross-boot retry budget** to main-session restart recovery **and** to the subagent-orphan recovery path so a genuinely wedged session can no longer death-loop the gateway across reboots. A session that can't be safely resumed is **quarantined after a bounded number of attempts** (transcript preserved) instead of re-triggering recovery on every boot.

## Changes

- **`SessionEntry`** gains `restartRecoveryAttempts`, `restartRecoveryQuarantinedAt`, `restartRecoveryQuarantineReason` (all optional, backwards compatible); reserved slot keys registered.
- **Mark phase** (main): increment `restartRecoveryAttempts` only on a **fresh** interruption (not already `abortedLastRun`), so re-marking within one boot does not double-charge the budget.
- **Main recovery gate** (`recoverStore`): if `restartRecoveryAttempts > MAX_RECOVERY_RETRIES`, **quarantine** — clear `abortedLastRun`, record `restartRecoveryQuarantinedAt` + reason `exceeded_restart_retry_budget`, WARN log. Transcript pointer preserved.
- **Subagent orphan path** (`recoverOrphanedSubagentSessions`): same cross-boot ceiling before resume; on accepted resume charge `restartRecoveryAttempts` once with prior===snapshot guard (no double-charge).
- **Budget reset on progress**: successful run (`status: "done"`) clears budget + quarantine via `derivePersistedSessionLifecyclePatch`.
- **Standalone repro**: `scripts/repro/issue-95750-restart-recovery-budget.mjs`.

## Behavioral contract

| Condition | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Wedged entry, 1st–3rd restart | Re-marked, resumed | Re-marked, resumed (`attempts` 1→3) |
| Same entry, 4th restart | Re-marked, resumed (loop) | **Quarantined**; `abortedLastRun=false`, `quarantinedAt` set, WARN logged |
| Successful run on the entry | n/a | budget + quarantine cleared |
| Subagent orphan over-budget | Resumed every boot | **Quarantined** same reason string |

## Evidence

**Exact commands after the full fix (main + subagent + repro):**
```
npx vitest run src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts src/agents/subagent-orphan-recovery.test.ts --project agents-core
node scripts/repro/issue-95750-restart-recovery-budget.mjs
```

**Captured output AFTER full fix:**
```
Test Files  2 passed (2)
     Tests  61 passed (61)

issue-95750-restart-recovery-budget: PASS
  ✓ over-budget→quarantine (transcript preserved)
  ✓ attempts=3 still resumes (boundary / negative control)
  ✓ accepted resume charges once; stale snapshot does not double-charge
  ✓ success→reset budget + quarantine
```

**Regression tests:**
- main: quarantine over-budget; resume at attempts=3; increment on fresh mark; no double-charge on re-mark; lifecycle clears on done
- subagent: still resumes within budget; over-budget quarantine preserves transcript; success records attempts; no double-charge on re-mark/stale snapshot
- repro script pure-logic: over-budget→quarantine, attempts=3 negative control, success→reset

target.title: fix(gateway): preserve abort after dispatch rejection
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #90999.

Users can see contradictory or missing terminal state when `chat.send` dispatch fails around abort/session-lifecycle timing. The bad windows are:

- abort already won, but a later post-dispatch rejection can overwrite the cached terminal result as an error;
- dispatch already failed, but a late `chat.abort` during fallback persistence can mask the real error as an abort;
- a queued followup was accepted, then an explicit abort won before dispatch rejection, and the accepted-followup branch could otherwise bypass the abort-preserve dedupe write;
- session lifecycle interruption after `chat.send` ACK can abort the controller without going through the normal `chat.abort` marker/broadcast path, leaving the client without a terminal `chat` event or keeping the session admission busy after terminal abort.

## Why This Change Was Made

The conflict refresh keeps current `main` session-admission, queued-followup, and dispatch-error lifecycle behavior, then makes terminal ownership explicit:

- if `chat.abort` already recorded the abort marker, preserve the abort terminal result, write the aborted dedupe, release session admission/active-run ownership before fallback persistence, and do not resurrect the run as an error;
- if a followup was already queued and no explicit abort marker owns the run, keep that accepted client run terminal;
- if dispatch/error owns the terminal state, close abortability before any awaited fallback persistence, clear stale abort state, cache the error, and broadcast the error;
- if lifecycle admission interrupts the run, do not treat a bare aborted signal as proof that a terminal abort was already broadcast.

The PR remains limited to `src/gateway/server-methods/chat.ts` and `src/gateway/server.chat.gateway-server-chat-b.test.ts`.

## User Impact

`chat.send` clients now receive one stable terminal outcome for these race windows. Same-run retries observe the correct cached terminal result, late abort does not rewrite a real dispatch error, lifecycle-interrupted sends still produce a terminal `chat` event, queued followup admission still terminalizes the accepted client run unless an explicit abort owns the run, and lifecycle operations are not held behind unrelated fallback transcript persistence after a terminal abort.

Related: #84176 and #84306.

target.title: fix(status): LINE /status intermittent no-response — fallback, timeout, and retry hardening
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On the LINE channel, `/status` sometimes returned no reply at all. The status text builder (`buildStatusText`) loads several runtime modules lazily via dynamic `import()`. If any of those imports rejects once — a transient module-resolution hiccup, a partial deploy, or a cold start — the loader cached the rejected promise, so every subsequent `/status` call failed and the command appeared to "do nothing."

## Why This Change Was Made

Two fixes:

1. **Retryable runtime loaders** (`src/status/status-text.ts`): the three dynamic loaders (`loadAgentHarnessSelectionRuntime`, `loadStatusSubagentsRuntime`, `loadStatusPluginHealthRuntime`) now reset their module-level promise to `null` inside `.catch()`, so a failed import is retried on the next call instead of permanently resolving to `undefined`. Callers already degrade gracefully when a loader returns `undefined`.
2. **Render timeout** (`src/auto-reply/reply/commands-status.ts`): `buildStatusReply` now races `buildStatusText` against a 10s timeout. If rendering stalls, the command returns a clear fallback (`⚠️ Status: timed out rendering response`) instead of hanging with no response. Real errors return `⚠️ Status: error rendering response (<message>)` and are logged via `logVerbose`.

Removed the now-unused lazy runtime barrels (`status.runtime.ts`, `status-message.runtime.ts`, `status-queue.runtime.ts`) and the `test:build:status-message-runtime` script.

## User Impact

`/status` (and `/status plugins`) on LINE reliably returns a response. Transient loader failures self-heal on the next request, and a slow render produces a readable timeout message rather than silence.

## Evidence

- Rebased onto current `upstream/main` (resolves the unrelated `check-test-types` failure that was a pre-existing discord test error on `main`).
- Added/adjusted tests: `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-status.test.ts` (timeout + throw fallback) and `src/status/status-text.test.ts` (loader retry cache). Typecheck and formatting verified locally.
- Fixes #94626.

## Summary

- Extends `claws update <claw-or-agent> --from <source> --yes` behind `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1` to apply every grouped owner in `openclaw.clawUpdateResult.v1`.
- Rebuilds and compares the read-only plan immediately before mutation, then advances root package/version/integrity provenance only after all owner executors succeed.
- Applies managed workspace file add/change/remove through fs-safe rooted I/O with source digest checks, destination compare-and-swap checks, ownership updates, and guarded rollback.
- Applies MCP add/change/remove through the validated config writer with create-only or expected-value CAS, including remote `sse` / `streamable-http` declarations and credential-free `auth: "oauth"`.
- Applies cron add/change/remove through gateway-owned APIs. Changes must converge on the stable Claw declaration key and existing scheduler id.
- Applies exact ClawHub skill/plugin package versions and updates package references. Removing a reference never implies shared uninstall; conflicting shared plugin version pins fail closed.
- Rolls completed owners back in reverse order when a later owner or root provenance fails. Thrown config/gateway writes and package installs without artifact rollback report `update_partial` instead of claiming atomicity.
- Keeps `--dry-run` read-only and requires explicit `--yes` consent.

This is the final implementation stage in the RFC series: it consumes the preceding read-only plan and adds explicit consent, owner-specific concurrency checks, compensation, and honest partial-state reporting.

Stack references:
- RFC: openclaw/rfcs#27
- Base PR: openclaw/openclaw#102959
- Control UI plugin management alignment: openclaw/openclaw#103176

## Ownership and Control UI alignment

Package references remain per-Claw provenance over shared skill/plugin artifacts. Update-time package removal releases only this Claw's reference. A plugin pinned to a different version by another Claw is not replaced. This keeps CLI lifecycle behavior aligned with the shared uninstall/reference-warning model used by the Control UI rather than creating a second plugin ownership system.

Portable MCP declarations continue to use the validated config surface. They are separate from the Control UI's curated connector shelf and do not persist headers, tokens, or completed OAuth state.

## Real behavior proof

Environment: WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 with isolated config and state.

An installed `@acme/update-proof@1.1.0` agent was previewed and updated to `1.2.0`:

```bash
openclaw claws update update-proof --from ./target-grouped --dry-run --json
openclaw claws update update-proof --from ./target-grouped --yes --json
openclaw claws status update-proof --json
```

The target changed the agent, added `SOUL.md` and `NOTES.md`, and added a remote `streamable-http` OAuth MCP server.

Observed:
- preview reported four unblocked grouped actions;
- apply returned `openclaw.clawUpdateResult.v1` with `status: "complete"`;
- both workspace files matched their target digests;
- the MCP ownership record was `complete` and live state was `present`;
- status reported version `1.2.0`, zero partial records, zero drift, and zero unresolved MCP references;
- the original `addedAtMs` was preserved while `updatedAtMs` advanced.

Cron convergence and exact package installer behavior are covered with injected gateway/installer tests to avoid mutating a developer gateway or shared plugin installation during local proof.

## Validation

- 133 Claw, CLI, lifecycle, config, executor, rollback, and end-to-end tests across 19 files
- non-incremental core TypeScript check: `tsgo -p tsconfig.json --noEmit --incremental false`
- real isolated grouped preview -> consented apply -> status round trip
- `git diff --check`

target.title: fix: skip setup-only channel plugins in outbound resolution and drain pending deliveries on qqbot reconnect
target.body:
## Summary

When the qqbot WebSocket reconnects after a session timeout (close code `4009`), `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` returns a setup-only plugin stub that lacks any send capability. This causes the `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` error, and all messages queued during the disconnection window are permanently lost.

## Root Cause

`resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` resolves the first matching plugin entry for a channel id without verifying that the entry actually has send capability (`outbound.sendText`, `message.send.text`, etc.). During qqbot WebSocket reconnection, a setup-only plugin entry (registered for configuration/pairing but not for message delivery) shadows the real sending plugin, causing the resolution to short-circuit with a non-functional stub.

Regression introduced in 2026.5.28 (commit `e932160`).

## Fix

### 1. Split outbound channel resolution into shared and delivery paths (`channel-resolution.ts`)

Add a `channelPluginCanSend()` predicate that checks for any of the 10 known send methods across both the legacy `outbound` adapter and the newer `message.send` adapter:

- `outbound.sendText / sendMedia / sendPayload / sendPoll / sendFormattedText / sendFormattedMedia`
- `message.send.text / media / payload / poll`

Instead of gating the shared `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` resolver (which would break action-only channel plugins that have `actions.handleAction` but no send capability), a new **`resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()`** resolver applies the send-capability guard exclusively for message delivery paths.

- **`resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()`**: Shared resolver — returns any matching plugin regardless of send capability, preserving resolution for action dispatch, target resolution, and other non-send callers.
- **`resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()`**: Delivery resolver — skips setup-only entries and only returns plugins that can actually send messages.
- **`resolveOutboundChannelMessageAdapter()`**: Updated to use the delivery resolver.
- **`message.ts`**: `sendMessage`/`sendPoll` updated to use the delivery resolver.

### 2. Align the direct delivery path with the operation-aware resolver (`deliver.ts`)

The preflight resolver was operation-aware, but the actual direct delivery handler reloaded the adapter capability-blind: `createChannelHandler` → `loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` → `loadChannelOutboundAdapter` resolved the first registry entry for the channel id (`createChannelRegistryLoader((entry) => entry.plugin.outbound)`) without checking send capability. A setup-only shell with a defined-but-non-send `outbound` (`{ deliveryMode: "direct" }`, no `sendText`) pinned ahead of the runtime sender therefore still shadowed the real adapter on the direct send path, throwing `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` even after preflight had selected a valid plugin. This also affected the reconnect drain path, which has no preflight.

`loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` now resolves through the same `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()` resolver as preflight (with `allowBootstrap`, operation `text`), so preflight and the actual direct delivery handler share one send-capability-aware resolution path. The previous manual bootstrap-and-retry is removed because the resolver's `allowBootstrap` performs the equivalent lazy materialize-then-retry. The generic registry loader and the CLI/SDK surfaces are left untouched.

### 3. Drain pending deliveries on qqbot reconnect (`extensions/qqbot/src/channel.ts`)

The `onReady` and `onResumed` gateway callbacks now call `drainPendingDeliveries()` from the plugin SDK delivery queue runtime, recovering messages that were queued while the WebSocket was disconnected. The drain is:

- Filtered by channel (`qqbot`) and account id, with a fallback for default-account entries where `accountId` may be `undefined`
- Deduplicated via `drainKey` to prevent concurrent drains
- Wrapped in try/catch so drain failures do not break the reconnection flow

### 4. Route the gateway poll handler through the operation-aware resolver (`src/gateway/server-methods/send.ts`)

The gateway `poll` handler still resolved its outbound plugin via the operation-blind `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()`, while `sendPoll` (`message.ts`) and the direct text delivery path (`deliver.ts`) already routed through the operation-aware `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()`. This left the gateway poll endpoint as the last surface where a setup-only / text-only first-match plugin could shadow a poll-capable runtime fallback and force a spurious `"unsupported poll channel"`, even though the new resolver test proves the poll-capable fallback should win.

The poll handler now resolves through `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery({ operation: "poll", allowBootstrap: true })`, mirroring the text delivery path. The `durationSeconds` / `isAnonymous` capability checks below the resolution now read from the same poll-capable plugin that serves `sendPoll`, so the capability gate and the actual send no longer disagree. The two non-poll resolver call sites in the same file (the `send` and `action` surfaces) are intentionally left on the shared resolver, since action-only plugins must still resolve without send capability.

## Tests

- `channel-resolution.test.ts`: setup-only plugin returns from shared resolver, action-only plugin resolves from shared but not delivery resolver, delivery resolver skips setup-only and returns sending fallback, legacy outbound adapter, poll-only outbound
- `deliver.test.ts`: new unmocked regression driving the real `deliverOutboundPayloads` → `createChannelHandler` → `loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` path with a pinned setup-only shell that exposes a defined non-send `outbound` plus an active send-capable fallback, asserting the send-capable adapter actually delivers (fails before the Fix 2 alignment with `"Outbound not configured"`, passes after)
- `channel.test.ts`: onReady drain, onResumed drain

Fixes #88955.


## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: After a QQ Bot WebSocket disconnect (session takeover / close code 4009), `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` returned a setup-only plugin stub instead of the runtime entry, causing `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` and dropping all pending deliveries.

- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw `2026.6.2` (commit `b90683e`, branch `fix/qqbot-reconnect-outbound-88955`), macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0. QQ Bot plugin `@openclaw/qqbot@2026.5.31-beta.4` with live QQ Bot credentials (appId `<redacted>`).

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  1. Built patched OpenClaw from fix branch: `pnpm build && npm pack --ignore-scripts`
  2. Installed globally: `npm install -g openclaw-2026.6.2.tgz` — confirmed version: `OpenClaw 2026.6.2 (b90683e)`
  3. Restarted gateway: `openclaw gateway restart`
  4. Observed qqbot plugin startup, WebSocket connection, and `Gateway ready` callback sequence in logs
  5. Verified normal QQ Bot C2C message round-trip: user sent "hello" → bot received → processed → replied with markdown (20 chars, 200 OK)
  6. Scanned full gateway log for `"Outbound not configured"` errors — zero matches
  7. Repeated restart cycle to confirm reconnect stability across multiple `Gateway ready` events

- **Evidence after fix**:
  ```
  # Patched OpenClaw installed and running
  $ openclaw --version
  OpenClaw 2026.6.2 (b90683e)

  # Gateway restart sequence — qqbot reconnects cleanly
  2026-06-02T22:38:53.727+08:00 [gateway] received SIGTERM; restarting
  ```

- **Observed result after fix**: The delivery resolver correctly skipped the setup-only plugin entry (which has no `sendText`/`sendMedia` methods) and resolved the runtime entry with full send capability. Zero occurrences of the `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` error across 18 reconnect cycles over a 4+ hour observation window. The shared resolver continued to return all plugin entries for non-send callers (action dispatch, target resolution), preserving action-only plugin compatibility.

- **Direct delivery path alignment (follow-up)**: A reviewer noted that the preflight fix did not cover the actual direct delivery handler construction, which reloaded the adapter capability-blind and could still let a pinned setup-only shell shadow the runtime sender. `loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` now routes through the same `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()` resolver as preflight. Verified locally on the fix branch (macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0): the new unmocked `deliver.test.ts` regression fails before the alignment (`Error: Outbound not configured for channel: matrix` thrown from `createChannelHandler`) and passes after; full focused suite green (`channel-resolution`, `message`, `message.channels`, `deliver`, qqbot `channel` — 169 tests passing), `pnpm tsgo:prod` and `pnpm tsgo:test` clean, `pnpm build` clean, `git diff --check` clean, lint clean.

- **Gateway poll resolver alignment (follow-up)**: A reviewer noted the gateway poll endpoint (`src/gateway/server-methods/send.ts`) still used the operation-blind `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()`, so a setup-only / text-only first match could shadow a poll-capable fallback and return `"unsupported poll channel"` despite a working poll plugin existing. The poll handler now routes through `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery({ operation: "poll", allowBootstrap: true })`, matching `sendPoll` and the direct text delivery path. Verified locally on the fix branch (macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0): a new gateway `send.test.ts` regression where the first-match plugin is a text-only shell (no `sendPoll`) and a poll-capable plugin is registered as the runtime fallback — the handler now skips the shell and dispatches the poll via the fallback (`messageId: poll-fallback-1`) instead of returning `"unsupported poll channel"`; the test fails under the old operation-blind resolver and passes after the change. Full gateway send suite green (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/send.test.ts` — 124 tests passing), `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:test:src` clean. The two non-poll resolver call sites in the same file are intentionally untouched.

- **What was not tested**:

  Live drain proof is not reproducible on the fixed build. The `drainReconnectPendingDeliveries()` mechanism (Fix 2) was verified via unit tests but not observed draining actual queued entries in a live environment. This is not an oversight — it is a structural consequence of the resolver fix (Fix 1) eliminating the only deterministic cause of pending qqbot entries. Code-level analysis confirms this:

  **How the delivery queue works** (`deliver.ts:1254-1280`): Every outbound delivery is write-ahead enqueued via `enqueueDelivery()` before any send attempt. On success, `ackDelivery()` removes the entry (`deliver.ts:1367`). On throw, `failDelivery()` bumps `retryCount` and **leaves it pending** (`delivery-queue-storage.ts:137-144`).

  **What created the pending entries in #88955**: The `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` throw fired from `createChannelHandler` (`deliver.ts:223-231`) when `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery` returned a setup-only plugin with no send methods. This throw occurs **outside** the per-payload try/catch (`deliver.ts:1451`), so it propagated to the queue-cleanup catch → `failDelivery` → entry left pending. The resolver fix eliminates this throw by filtering setup-only entries via `channelPluginCanSend()`.

  **Why transient QQ API failures also do not create pending entries**: The qqbot engine **swallows** HTTP/network errors into returned `{error}` result objects instead of throwing (`outbound.ts:301-304, 313-318`). The delivery core text branch records "sent" purely on `deliveredResults.length > 0` with no message-id identity gate (`deliver.ts:1772-1778`), so a swallowed engine error yields a "sent" outcome → `ackDelivery` → entry removed, not pending.

  **The drain's real value**: It is a belt-and-suspenders safeguard for the **upgrade path** — entries left pending (with `lastError: "Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"`) by an unfixed build are drained immediately after a fixed gateway reconnects. The `bypassBackoff` predicate explicitly matches this exact error string (`/outbound not configured/i`), ensuring these entries skip retry backoff and are retried on the first reconnect event. If the retry still fails (e.g., the plugin is genuinely misconfigured), `isPermanentDeliveryError` (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts:79`) moves the entry to `failed/` — no infinite retry loop. `MAX_RETRIES` is also enforced before the bypass branch (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts:544`). The drain also covers the narrow crash-in-enqueue-to-ack window handled by `recoverPendingDeliveries` at startup (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts:604`). The drain selection filter (`channel === "qqbot"` + account id match + bypassBackoff for `"Outbound not configured"`, `channel.test.ts:90-152`) and the reconnect-drain integration logic (`delivery-queue.reconnect-drain.test.ts`) are exercised by 35 unit tests (all passing).

  **Seeded pending-drain proof**: To validate the drain recovery path end-to-end, a pending delivery entry was manually seeded into the SQLite delivery queue to simulate the upgrade scenario (entries left by an unfixed build):

  1. Inserted a pending entry: `id=seeded-drain-test-001`, `channel=qqbot`, `accountId=default`, `lastError="Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"`, `retry_count=1`
  2. Restarted gateway: `openclaw gateway restart`
  3. Observed recovery sequence in logs:

  ```
  00:30:00.353 [gateway] http server listening (8 plugins: ..., qqbot, ...; 1.9s)
  00:30:00.987 [delivery-recovery] Found 1 pending delivery entries — starting recovery
  00:30:01.567 [qqbot] [qqbot:api] <<< Status: 200 OK
  00:30:02.703 [delivery-recovery] Recovered delivery seeded-drain-test-001 on qqbot
  00:30:02.703 [delivery-recovery] Delivery recovery complete: 1 recovered, 0 failed, 0 skipped (max retries), 0 deferred (backoff)
  00:30:02.816 [qqbot] [default] WebSocket connected
  00:30:02.952 [qqbot] [qqbot:default] Gateway ready
  ```

  4. Verified entry removed from DB: `SELECT count(*) FROM delivery_queue_entries WHERE channel='qqbot' AND status='pending'` → **0**
  5. Zero `"Outbound not configured"` errors after restart

  **Key observation**: The `0 deferred (backoff)` in the recovery summary confirms the `bypassBackoff` predicate (`/outbound not configured/i`) correctly matched the seeded entry's `lastError`, allowing immediate retry without waiting for backoff. The entry was successfully delivered (HTTP 200) and acked (removed from queue).

  **Note**: The startup `recoverPendingDeliveries` path (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts:604`) executed before the qqbot `onReady` callback (`00:30:00.987` vs `00:30:02.952`), so startup recovery handled the entry before the reconnect drain fired. Both paths share the same underlying drain logic and bypass predicates; the startup path simply runs first. A naturally-occurring live drain on the `onReady` path cannot be reliably reproduced because the fix removes the deterministic failure that created those entries, and startup recovery pre-empts the reconnect drain for entries present at boot. Multi-shard configurations were not tested.

target.title: [Bug]: Signal quoted replies can lose quoted context in BodyForAgent
target.body:
## Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

## Beta release blocker
No

## Summary
Signal quoted-reply context can be extracted into `ReplyToBody` / related metadata while `BodyForAgent` remains only the new ambiguous message body, so agent-facing paths that rely on `BodyForAgent` can miss the quoted target.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Configure the Signal channel and receive an inbound Signal message.
2. From Signal, quote/reply to that message with an ambiguous body such as `Did this get done?`.
3. Inspect the inbound context handed to the agent/prompt-building path.

## Expected behavior
The agent-facing input reliably includes the quoted target, either as a clear quoted block in `BodyForAgent` or through another prompt-builder-guaranteed surface that survives retries/session handoff. A useful rendered shape is:

```text
Quoted Signal reply context from sender:
> original quoted message

Did this get done?
```

Session retries, queued followups, and handoff paths should preserve the quote-enhanced agent-facing context. Plain non-quoted Signal messages should remain unchanged, and normalization should not duplicate the quote block.

## Actual behavior
`ReplyToBody` / quote metadata can exist, but `BodyForAgent` can be just the ambiguous new body, for example `Did this get done?`. Paths that consume the current message body directly may therefore omit the quoted target even though the adapter extracted it elsewhere.

## OpenClaw version
Current `main` before the proposed fix, and observed against a recent npm-installed OpenClaw runtime with the Signal adapter. Exact released build: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

## Operating system
Linux/macOS deployments are affected by the Signal adapter shape; exact OS for a minimal upstream repro: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

## Install method
npm global and source checkout investigation

## Model
NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

## Provider / routing chain
NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

## Additional provider/model setup details
NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

## Logs
```shell
NOT_ENOUGH_INFO
```

## Screenshots, recordings, and evidence
Local source investigation shows the Signal adapter computes visible quote context and stores it on reply metadata fields, while the agent-facing body can remain the new message body. A local post-update workaround inlined the quote into the agent body with the quoted-block shape shown above.

## Impact and severity
Affected: Signal users sending quoted replies to an OpenClaw agent.
Severity: Medium to high, because short replies such as `Did this get done?` or `what about this?` can become unintelligible to the model.
Frequency: Whenever a quoted Signal reply depends on the quoted target and the consuming path sees only `BodyForAgent`.
Consequence: The agent may answer the wrong item or ignore the intended quoted context.

## Additional information
Related but non-duplicate: #98234 covers Signal reply-session initialization conflict retry/drop behavior. This issue is specifically about preserving quoted Signal context in the agent-facing body/text. Older Signal quote issues/PRs cover native quote support or queued structured metadata, but this report is the narrower `BodyForAgent` agent-facing context gap.

target.title: fix(reply): add per-hook timeout with timer cleanup in combineBeforeDeliverHooks (#103684)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a channel `beforeDeliver` hook never resolves or rejects, `waitForIdle()`
blocks forever. The `sendChain` is permanently stuck, subsequent replies are
never delivered, and the lane stays blocked. Reported on WhatsApp with
`2026.6.11` / Node v24.18.0 / Raspberry Pi.

Fixes #103684.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added `beforeDeliverTimeoutMs` option (default 30s) to `ReplyDispatcherOptions`.
In `createReplyDispatcher`, each `beforeDeliver` hook is wrapped with a
`Promise.race` deadline — a hung hook returns `null` (cancellation),
`waitForIdle()` resolves, and the lane recovers. Channels with known slow
hooks can configure a longer deadline. Set `0` to disable.

Timer cleanup uses `try/finally` so rejection and fulfillment both clear the
scheduled timer. Timeouts emit a `logWarn` so operators can detect the event.

## User Impact

**Before:** hung channel hook permanently blocks lane, requires restart +
manual `sessions.json` editing
**After:** dispatcher unblocks after timeout, lane recovers automatically.
Timeout is configurable per channel via `beforeDeliverTimeoutMs`.

## Evidence

Branch: `fix/103684-before-deliver-timeout` | Base: `upstream/main`

### Lane recovery proof (simulated WhatsApp scenario from #103684)

```
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof/before-deliver-timeout.mts

=== #103733 lane recovery proof ===

── Scenario: hung beforeDeliver → timeout → lane recovery ──
  Hook hung:        true
  waitForIdle:      true (2057ms)
  Cancelled count:  1 (Real reply)
  Delivered count:  1
  Delivered:        ["Follow-up message after recovery"]

  VERDICT:
    Recovery (waitForIdle < 10s): PASS
    Hung msg cancelled:            PASS
    Next msg delivered:             PASS
    Lane unblocked:                 PASS

  OVERALL: ALL PASSED
```

### Regression tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/before-deliver.test.ts

 ✓ cancels delivery before queueing when transformReplyPayload returns null
 ✓ cancels delivery when beforeDeliver returns null
 ... 5 more passing ...

 Test Files  1 passed (1)  Tests  7 passed (7)
```

### Diff summary

```
src/auto-reply/reply/reply-dispatcher.ts | 28 ++ (timeout wrapper + option)
scripts/proof/before-deliver-timeout.mts | 65 ++ (lane recovery proof)
```

What was not tested: live WhatsApp channel with real bot credentials. The
proof script exercises `createReplyDispatcher` with the exact `Promise.race`
deadline pattern, proving `waitForIdle()` settles and a subsequent dispatcher
delivers normally — the same sequence a real lane recovery follows.

- [x] I understand what the code does
- [x] Change is focused and does not mix unrelated concerns

target.title: fix(memory): drop bare heartbeat acks (with decoration) from dreaming corpus
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves Heartbeat acknowledgements that are not the exact string `HEARTBEAT_OK` leak into the dreaming session corpus as low-confidence snippets, where they crowd out real content in the Light and REM phases and produce illegible "A memory trace surfaced, but details were unavailable in this run." ghost entries in `DREAMS.md`. ## Root Cause `sanitizeSessionText` in `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/session-files.ts` dropped an assistant reply only when `normalized === "HEARTBEAT_OK"`. Decoration variants of the bare token — trailing punctuation (`HEARTBEAT_OK.`, `HEARTBEAT_OK!!!`), markdown/HTML wrappers (`**HEARTBEAT_OK**`, `HEARTBEAT_OK`) — did not match and were indexed. ## Changes - Reuse the canonical `stripHeartbeatToken` parser (already used by the heartbeat filter) via the memory-host-sdk runtime facade. - `sanitizeSessionText` now drops an assistant message only when, after removing the token, **no letter or digit survives** (`/[\p{L}\p{N}]/u`) — i.e. it is the bare token plus pure punctuation/markup decoration. - Tests: bare token and decoration variants are dropped; genuine prose that merely contains the token is preserved. ## Scope / Boundary (updated after review) An earlier revision reused `isHeartbeatOkResponse`, whose 300-char acknowledgement budget classified any short reply containing the token as an ack. As the review noted, that over-drops legitimate content — e.g. `HEARTBEAT_OK means the periodic check succeeded.` would be silently removed from indexed memory. This revision narrows the drop to **decoration only**: - We deliberately do **not** gate on heartbeat ownership via the preceding user message: the existing code comment rejects that cross-message coupling because a real user could spoof the heartbeat prompt text, and there is no per-message heartbeat provenance at this ingestion boundary. - Any assistant reply that carries real prose beyond the token — including non-ASCII prose — is preserved. - Token-free natural-language acknowledgements remain out of scope (they are a prompt/model-compliance concern, and were never matched by the previous exact-string rule either). Issue 1 in the report (deleted/reset transcripts ingested by dreaming) is also intentionally unchanged: those archives are deliberately retained for `memory_search` (see the comment and the `indexes usage-counted reset/deleted archives` test in `session-files.ts`); the broader ingestion scope is tracked in #72611. ## Evidence **1. Focused tests (RED before, GREEN after)** — a new regression test preserves a short genuine token-bearing reply; it failed on the previous revision and passes now: ``` $ npx vitest run packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/session-files.test.ts -t "buildSessionEntry" Test Files 1 passed (1) Tests 12 passed | 28 skipped (40) ``` **2. Real behavior proof** — a standalone script (not a test harness) runs the actual `buildSessionEntry` corpus builder on a realistic heartbeat transcript and prints the resulting corpus content: ``` Assistant message -> corpus verdict: DROPPED "HEARTBEAT_OK" DROPPED "HEARTBEAT_OK." DROPPED "HEARTBEAT_OK!!!" DROPPED "**HEARTBEAT_OK**" DROPPED "HEARTBEAT_OK" KEPT "HEARTBEAT_OK means the periodic check succeeded." KEPT "HEARTBEAT_OK 表示这一轮心跳检查已通过。" KEPT "The digest job failed because the API token expired." --- Resulting corpus content --- Assistant: HEARTBEAT_OK means the periodic check succeeded. Assistant: HEARTBEAT_OK 表示这一轮心跳检查已通过。 Assistant: The digest job failed because the API token expired. RESULT: PASS — bare/decorated acks dropped, genuine prose preserved. ``` - The 3 `listSessionTranscriptCorpusEntriesForAgent` failures observed locally are pre-existing Windows path-casing issues (`c:\...` vs `C:\...`); they fail identically on a clean `origin/main` baseline with this change stashed, so they are unrelated to this PR. Related: #103720 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

target.title: [Feature]: System prompt architecture refactor — from fragmented rules to unified cognitive framework
target.body:
### Summary

Refactor OpenClaw's system prompt from a "20+ fragmented rule blocks stitched together" design into a 3-tier architecture (**core cognitive framework + dynamic injection + on-demand reference**), releasing 80%+ of attention budget so the same underlying model stops "getting dumber" on real tasks.

### Problem to solve

After six months of daily use with the same model backend (deepseek-v4-pro), I consistently observe that **decision quality on OpenClaw is significantly lower than the same model on specialized agents (e.g., OpenCode)**. Even after injecting a structured thinking methodology through USER.md / extraSystemPrompt, the agent still:

1. **Frequently loses context, skips steps, and loops on wrong tool choices in multi-step tasks**
2. **Makes noticeably "dumb" decisions** — e.g., single-threading work that obviously should use sessions_spawn, guessing answers instead of reading docs first
3. **Injected methodology instructions are completely ineffective, sometimes even making the agent appear more confused**

### Root cause analysis

After fully reviewing `src/agents/system-prompt.ts`, the rendered system prompt is approximately **30k-40k tokens**. Breaking down by function:

| Category | Representative Sections | Share | Contribution to task completion |
|----------|------------------------|-------|--------------------------------|
| **Framework management** | Control, Self-Update, Heartbeats, Silent Replies, Sandbox, Sub-Agent Delegation, ACP Harness | ~25% | Zero — these are runtime plumbing the agent shouldn't need to know |
| **Channel adaptation** | Messaging (including full Telegram rich-text spec), Embed UI, Voice, Reactions | ~20% | Near-zero — all non-current channels are pure noise |
| **Context injection** | Project Context (SOUL/AGENTS/BOOTSTRAP etc.) | ~35% | Partial (varies by user) |
| **Core behavior** | Execution Bias (7 bullets), Safety, Tool Call Style, Tooling | ~20% | The only part that actually does work |

**Key findings:**

1. **45% of token budget is spent on content irrelevant to "getting the task done."** The model assigns roughly equal attention weight to all instructions in the system prompt. These fragmented but high-volume management/channel rules dominate the attention pool, leaving minimal cognitive resources for "how to actually do the task well."

2. **The only section resembling a "framework" — Execution Bias — is merely 7 if-then rules** ("vary query on empty results," "don't poll sessions_list"). There is **no methodology-level guidance** telling the agent *what kind of thinking process to follow* for any arbitrary task.

3. **Safety/permission constraints should be enforced at the code layer, not through prompt soft-constraints.** "Don't bypass safeguards," "don't self-update without explicit request" — the agent cannot be stopped by prompt text if it actually wants to violate these. Similarly, message formatting and channel rules are framework-level concerns that shouldn't occupy the agent's mental space.

### Proposed solution

**Core idea: Give the agent a cognitive operating system, not an operations manual.**

#### Three-tier prompt architecture

```
[Tier 1 — Always Injected] Core principles + cognitive framework
     (~3-5k tokens, every line is a "how to think" principle)

[Tier 2 — Dynamically Injected] Current channel/session context
     Injected by framework only when relevant; transparent to agent

[Tier 3 — On-Demand Reference] Channel rules, tool details
     Agent proactively loads via read("docs/...") when needed
```

#### Code-layer enforcement (remove from prompt)

| Current prompt instruction | Proposed code enforcement |
|---|---|
| "Do not invent commands" | Return error for unknown commands |
| "Never execute /approve through exec" | exec tool filters /approve |
| "Only explicit user request for self-update" | update operation requires tool-layer permission check |
| HEARTBEAT_OK reply format | Framework auto-detects heartbeat and responds |
| Silent reply token rules | Framework handles silence logic internally |
| "Obey stop/pause/audit" | Hard interrupts at tool layer, not prompt soft-constraint |

#### Tier 1 example (replacing current fragments)

```
## Cognitive Framework
For any task, reason through this process:

1. Intent extraction — What does the user actually need? Hidden constraints?
2. Strategy generation — Decompose into subtasks, select optimal tools, identify dependencies
3. Execution & verification — Verify each step's result before proceeding, build evidence chain
4. Global check — All aspects of the original need covered? Any gaps or side effects?
5. Delivery loop — Deliver result + evidence, or state gaps and next steps

## Behavioral Principles
- Information first: verify/ask before guessing, never assume
- Minimum viable step: one verifiable action per turn
- Failure handling: change strategy on empty/error results, not repeat; report to user after 3 failures
- Impact assessment: confirm no existing state is disrupted before modifying
```

### Alternatives considered

1. **User injects methodology via USER.md / extraSystemPrompt** (tried, ineffective) — The root cause is that existing fragmented rules dominate attention. New instructions can only compete for remaining budget and cannot override the noise effect of old instructions.
2. **Channel-split agents** (partially adopted) — Mitigates channel adaptation noise but cannot address the 25% framework management instruction problem.
3. **OpenAI/Anthropic prompt caching** (partially in use in OpenClaw already) — Performance optimization, does not address structural fragmentation.

### Impact

- **Affected**: All OpenClaw users (non-English users disproportionately affected — fragmented instructions create more interference in non-native-language contexts)
- **Severity**: High — directly impacts agent usability and user trust
- **Frequency**: Every complex multi-step task triggers this
- **Consequence**: Model capabilities suppressed by prompt noise; users forced to switch to other tools for complex work

### Evidence/examples

- Same model (deepseek-v4-pro) performs significantly better on OpenCode than OpenClaw (tested: multi-file refactoring, API integration, project scaffolding)
- OpenCode's system prompt is ~20-30% the size of OpenClaw's, entirely focused on the coding domain with zero channel adaptation / framework management layers
- Anthropic's system prompt design guide explicitly recommends "load core persona first, supplement task details on demand"
- Full source analysis based on line-by-line review of `src/agents/system-prompt.ts`

### Additional information

- `src/agents/system-prompt.ts` is ~1441 lines / 65 KB and already provides provider plugin hooks (sectionOverrides, stablePrefix, dynamicSuffix), making refactoring cost relatively manageable
- Suggest `promptMode: "minimal"` be further stripped to exclude Messaging/Embed UI/TTS/Reactions sections
- Backward compatible: keep existing extraSystemPrompt injection paths, toggle old/new prompts via promptMode

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
